313/1
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
PAPER 1
JULY/AUGUST 2026
21/2 Hours
MARKING SCHEME
 1. (a) Historical books in the old testament
 i. Joshua
 ii. Judges
 iii. Ruth
 iv. 1 Samuel
 v. 2 Samuel
 vi. 1 kings
 vii. 2 kings
 viii. 1 chronicles
 ix. 2 chronicles
 x. Ezra
 xi. Nehemiah
 xii. Esther
 6×1=6mks
 (b)Why the bible is considered as the word of God
 i. The authors who wrote the bible were under the influence of/ inspired by the Holy
 spirit
 ii. It reveals Gods character /attribute/nature
 iii. God communicates to human beings through the bible / people get God’s guidance
 from the bible.
 iv. God was involved directly in the writing of some parts of the Bible/Ten
 commandments.
 v. It contains prophecies / promises made by God to human beings.
 vi. The bible reveals the person of Jesus Christ who is the son of God to humankind.
 vii. The bible has power to transform peoples lives / source of moral values
 viii. It is a record of Gods work / action/ events
 ix. The bible has remained relevant for all generations
 7×1=7mks
 (c) Ways in which the bible is misused in Kenya Today.
 i. The bible is used to take oaths in courts / offices by individuals who may not be
 believers / are not eligible
 ii. Some people use the bible to threaten others/ administer curses
 iii. Some people use the bible as a tool of trade / enrich themselves.
 iv. It is kept in places associated with evil/brothels.
 v. It is being used in cults / witchcraft to mislead people
 vi. Some people do not read the bible for spiritual growth / do not obey it
 vii. Some people keep the bible for display / it is neglected
 viii. Some people use the bible like an ordinary textbook.
 ix. Some people, mishandle the bible by writing in it / tearing pages
 x. Some people use specific Bible verses to support / realize their selfish
 ends/manipulations
 7×1=7mks
2. (a) How God prepared Moses for his future role as a leader of the Israelites.
 i. God saved Moses from death – Moses was born when Hebrew baby boys were
 being thrown in River Nile/killed but God saved him.
 ii. Moses was adopted from pharaoh’s daughter at the palace- this was Gods design to
 ensure that Moses underwent education/acquired leadership skills.
 iii. Nursed by his mother – pharaoh daughter employed Moses mother as a nurse this
 gave the mother an opportunity to bring up/train Moses in Jewish traditions/ Moses
 knew he was an Israelites not an Egyptian.
 iv. Escape from Egypt – this was Gods plan to expose Moses to the routes in the
 wilderness which he would use later to lead the Israelites.
 v. Life in wilderness - the harsh desert life in the wilderness enabled Moses to acquire
 perseverance/patience/endurance/virtues he would use to lead the Israelites.
 vi. Shepherd life – Moses became a shepherd looking after the flock of his father in
 law, a responsibility that prepared him to lead the people.
 vii. Marriage/family life – becoming a family man was another way of training Moses
 for leadership. A husband/father is expected to be responsible.
 viii. During the call of Moses– God revealed himself to Moses / revealed His name /
 identified Himself as God of the ancestors of Moses.
 ix. Moses visit to Goshen – God enabled Moses to witness the problems of the
 Israelites in the land of Goshen/was aware of their suffering.
 x. Empowerment – God empowered Moses to perform miracles.
 xi. Spokesman – God gave Moses a Spokesman/Aaron who would speak on behalf of
 Moses to Pharaoh
 xii. God’s assurance – God promised Moses protection / assured him that he would
 bring the people up to the mountain.
 7×1=7mks
(b) The conditions that God gave to the Israelites during the renewal of the covenant
(Exodus 34 : 11-28 )
 i. The Israelites were not to make covenants with the inhabitants of the land of
 Canaan /Canaanites /Hittites / Perizites.
 ii. The Israelites were to tear down the alters / idols that the inhabitants of the land
 used.
 iii. They were not to intermarry with the inhabitants in the land of Canaan.
 iv. They were not to make any graven /molten gods/idols/images.
 v. The Israelites were to keep the feast of unleavened bread for seven days
 vi. They were to dedicate their first born sons / first born of animals to God.
 vii. When going into the presence of God / to worship God, they were to ensure
 they had something to offer to God / not to appear before God empty hands
 viii. They were to keep the Sabbath day holy / work to be done on six days/observe
 the law of sabbath
 ix. All the Israelites men were to appear before God three times a year.
 x. The sacrifice of the feast of Passover was not to be left until morning.
 7×1=7mks
(c) Reasons why Christians should not commit murder.
 i. Christians should not commit murder because life is scared / should not be
 destroyed by any one / life belongs to God
 ii. Killing brings hatred /revenge/ ill feelings among people/ undermines peace/
 harmony in the society.
 iii. It terminates the continuity of a family.
 iv. It brings poverty if the person killed is the bread winner.
 v. Murder / killing others cause fear / anxiety in the society / people become
 insecure.
 vi. It creates sadness / misery / sorrow to the relatives of the deceased.
 vii. Murder leads to life imprisonment.
 viii. Murder undermines the Christians virtue of love / against God’s principle of
 forgiveness.
 ix. It is disobedience of God’s law / attracts God’s punishment.
 x. It undermines the victims’ right to life / against human rights.
 6×1=6mks
3. (a)The failures of King Saul
 i. He offered the burnt offerings instead of waiting for Samuel to do it
 ii. He lacked patience to wait for Samuel who was to offer burnt offering to God.
 iii. He disobeyed Gods command to destroy the Amalekites completely by sparing the
 life of King Agag
 iv. He spared the best of the animals instead of destroying them.
 v. He lost faith/trust in God/divination/necromancy/consulted a medium.
 vi. He wanted to kill David / was jealous of David.
 vii. He was deceitful to the servant of God.
 6×1=6mks
 (b) The achievements of David as King of Israel.
 i. David conquered and defeated the enemies of Israel
 ii. He expanded the geographical boundaries of Israel.
 iii. He captured Jerusalem from the Jebusites.
 iv. He made Jerusalem the capital city of Israel
 v. He made Jerusalem a religious center by bringing the ark of the covenant there
 vi. He made peace treaties with his neighbors/diplomacy.
 vii. He composed psalms which are used during worship.
 viii. He united the twelve tribes of Israel under one ruler.
 ix. He made preparations for the construction of the temple.
 7×1=7mks
 (c) Reasons why Christians build churches
 i. Churches are used for worshipping God.
 ii. They signify God’s presence / house of God
 iii. They are used for meetings / a place of gathering
 iv. Religious functions take place there
 v. They are places where members receive religious instruction / preaching
 vi. As a sign of prestige / recognition /identification
 vii. To demonstrate their faith in the existence of God
 viii. To follow the traditions of the old testament teachings on the use of the temple as a
 house of God
 ix. It can be used as a place of refuge in times of danger / calamity
 7×1=7mks
4. (a) Differences between true and false prophets
 i. True prophets were called by God whereas false prophets did not have divine call /
 raised themselves.
 ii. True prophets received messages from God while the false prophets, prophesied
 out of their own minds/ imaginations.
 iii. The prophecies of the true prophets were fulfilled while those of false prophets,
 were not fulfilled
 iv. True prophets faced opposition/rejection while false prophets were liked by the
 people.
 v. True prophets spoke with authority from God /were fearless while the false
 prophets depended on their own authority / self confidence
 vi. True prophets were not paid for their work whereas false prophets received pay for
 their services.
 vii. The true prophets preached about God’s judgement for sin whereas false prophets
 preached peace where there was
 Download thisno
 andpeace/sooth Sayers.
 viii. True prophets called people to worship the true God while false prophets promoted
 idolatry.
 ix. True prophets called people to the covenant way of life /repentance while false
 prophets were silent/ tolerated the evils/led people astray.
 7×1=7mks
 (b)Reasons why prophet Amos was against the way the Israelites worshipped God
 during his time.
 i. The Israelites had neglected Yahweh their true God.
 ii. They worshipped God as well as Baal / practiced syncretism.
 iii. Their worship was insincere / had no inner faith.
 iv. They were impatient during the worship ceremonies / wanted to go back to their
 businesses
 v. They had many empty ceremonial festivals /feasts
 vi. They defiled the place of worship by drinking wine there.
 vii. The worshippers were not righteous / they had mistreated fellow Israelites which
 was against God’s teaching.
 viii. They gave sacrifices /offerings as a show off / pride / not for love of God
 ix. They built high places for worship of idols.
 7×1=7mks
 (c) Challenges that the church leaders in Kenya encounter while carrying out their
 work.
 i. Church leaders lack adequate funds to carry out their duties.
 ii. Lack of unity / co-operation from the members of the church
 iii. Some lack adequate skills for carrying out their work.
 iv. They face opposition from false prophets / cults / devil worship
 v. Poor means of transport that makes it difficult to reach some areas.
 vi. Permissiveness / moral decadence in the society
 vii. There is insecurity in some parts of the country / religious intolerance
 viii. Harsh climatic conditions / hostile environment hinder effective evangelism.
 ix. Negative influence from mass media / pornography.
 x. Rivalry among the leaders themselves
 xi. Political interference in their work.
 xii. Some suffer rejection / separation from their families.
 xiii. Some fail to lead exemplary lives.
 6×1=6mks
5. (a) The stages followed during the renewal of the covenant at the time of Nehemiah.
 i. The people gathered in the public square in Jerusalem.
 ii. The priest Ezra read the law to the people.
 iii. The people constructed makeshift tents / shelters to celebrate the feasts of the
 booths.
 iv. They performed repentance gestures of raising / lowering their hands
 v. There was national day of confession / fasting as they wore sack clothes
 vi. Ezra led people in prayer of confession
 vii. They sealed the covenant by signing an agreement under the leadership of
 Nehemiah and the priest.
 viii. The people promised not to go against the mosaic law.
 ix. The re-distribution of the people in Jerusalem and country side.
 8×1=8mks
 (b) Reasons why Nehemiah carried out religious reforms in Judah
 i. To preserve the identity of the Jews as people of God.
 ii. To separate the Jews from foreign influence.
 iii. To purify the temple that had been defiled by keeping a foreigner.
 iv. To reinstate the services of the Levites as priests in the temple.
 v. To restore the tithing system that had been forgotten for the upkeep of the Temple.
 vi. To ensure that the Sabbath day was free from business activities.
 vii. In order to cleanse the Jews who had intermarried with foreigners / exposed to
 idolatry.
 6×1=6mks
 (c) Lesson from the renewal of the covenant by Nehemiah
 i. Christians should ask for their sins to be forgiven.
 ii. They should lead righteous lives.
 iii. Christians should demonstrate humility.
 iv. Christians should always pray to God.
 v. They should avoid groups that can negatively influence their faith in God.
 vi. They should teach others the word of God.
 vii. They should set aside a day for worship.
 viii. They should respect the church as a place for prayer.
 6×1=6mks
6. (a) The role of healers in traditional African communities.
 i. Healers identify the causes of various sicknesses / diseases/illnesses.
 ii. They offer herbal medicine to the patients for physical / psychological healing.
 iii. They assist in dispelling witchcraft / sorcery / magic.
 iv. They perform cleansing rituals for individuals.
 v. They give herbs to increase fertility in people / animals / land.
 vi. Healers avert effects of curses in the society.
 vii. They train other people to become healers/offer knowledge on herbal medicine /
 practical application.
 viii. They guide and counsel people on matters of health.
 7×1=7mks
(b) The significance of rituals performed during initiation ceremonies in traditional
 African communities.
 i. Prayers are said for protection of initiates from evil spirits/ blessings from God
 ii. Singing and dancing is done for entertainment / educating the initiates.
 iii. Sacrifices are made to ask for protection / blessings from God.
 iv. Libations are poured to appease the ancestors / invoke their blessings upon the
 initiates.
 v. Initiates are smeared with mud to make the body numb for less pain / disguise the
 initiates.
 vi. Feasting is carried out to celebrate the courage of the initiates / express joy.
 vii. Gifts are given to congratulate the initiates.
 viii. Seclusion – the initiates are secluded in order to be educated / well fed / protect
 them from evil eyes.
 ix. Washing in a stream of water for cleansing / marking new beginnings.
 x. Wearing of protective charms to keep the initiates safe from evil.
 7×1=7mks
 c. Reasons why the government has outlawed the practice of female genital mutilation in
 Kenya.
 i. It may lead to early marriage / school drop out.
 ii. Female genital mutilation causes complications during child birth.
 iii. Female genital mutilation is a dehumanizing experience / lowers human dignity.
 iv. It causes psychological challenges / trauma / stress
 v. It denies women the human right of enjoying sex.
 vi. It is an outdated / not adding value
 vii. It may lead to death due to overbleeding
viii. The practice may lead to infection / sexual transmitted infections/STD’S.
 6×1=6mks
